findings.locator: Primary abstract methods/results unless selected publisher passages stated
findings.context: Specified habit/planning study; no generic cross-task transfer
findings.exposure: Repeat selected behavior in stable daily context
findings.comparator: Earlier scores/variation in adherence; no randomized untreated counterfactual
findings.measurement: Subset of self-report habit automaticity items
findings.timing: 84days; some modeled asymptotes beyond observed period
findings.result: Automaticity increased on average with heterogeneous trajectories and model fits.
findings.limitations: Self-selection, shared self-report and successful-fit selection; cannot infer causal rate/threshold or exact latent habit propensity. Missing one occasion was not materially disruptive in this sample.

findings.locator: Primary abstract methods/results unless selected publisher passages stated
findings.context: Specified habit/planning study; no generic cross-task transfer
findings.exposure: Routine-based cue for selected daily nutrition behavior
findings.measurement: Daily self-reported automaticity and plan enactment
findings.result: No between-condition differences in automaticity or enactment were detected.
findings.limitations: Nondetection not equivalence; both conditions receive planning. Does not prove either outperforms no planning or isolate repeated behavior.

findings.locator: Primary abstract methods/results unless selected publisher passages stated
findings.context: Specified habit/planning study; no generic cross-task transfer
findings.exposure: Plan enactment and repeated behavior over time
findings.comparator: Own baseline, not an untreated group
findings.timing: 84days; median59days only among successful habit formers
findings.result: Both groups increased automaticity/enactment; repetition predicted automaticity.
findings.limitations: Prediction/pre-post change not randomized repetition. Conditional learner duration not a universal causal time constant.

findings.context: Specified habit/planning study; no generic cross-task transfer
findings.measurement: Outcome-devaluation sensitivity, not self-report habit propensity
findings.timing: Task-specific extended training and later devaluation tests
findings.result: Overtraining did not increase inflexible habit expression in the reported attempts.
findings.limitations: OUTSIDE daily-context operation; devaluation task may be insensitive and impaired goal-directed control can mimic habit. Failure not proof no habits form.

findings.locator: Primary abstract methods/results unless selected publisher passages stated
findings.context: Specified habit/planning study; no generic cross-task transfer
findings.exposure: Form specified if-then plan linking critical cue and response
findings.measurement: Cue accessibility, cue-response linkage and word-search performance; exact priming cell contrasts not fully extracted
findings.result: Plan condition improved critical-task speed and report describes enhanced cue accessibility/linkage with statistical mediation.
findings.limitations: Performance and cue accessibility are not the exact associative-strength contrast; mediated regression not identified transmitted pathway. Full priming controls/measurement need extraction before direction on PSY-072.

findings.locator: Primary abstract methods/results unless selected publisher passages stated
findings.design: Two studies: measured goal-strength interaction and goal-activation manipulation
findings.population: Goal/task participants described in source abstract
findings.context: Specified habit/planning study; no generic cross-task transfer
findings.exposure: Implementation intention under differing goal strength/activation
findings.measurement: Goal attainment/performance, not direct cue-response association strength
findings.timing: Study-specific goal activation and later behavior
findings.result: Planning benefits occurred with strong/activated relevant goals, not weak or neutral-goal conditions.
findings.limitations: Measured strength is between-person association; activation manipulation distinct. OUTSIDE exact PSY-072 target. No independent moderation of REL-PSY-036 inferred.

happeningTypes.name: Repeat a selected behavior in response to a declared recurring cue
happeningTypes.description: Deliberately repeat a specified selected behavior when a declared routine/time/context cue occurs. Identity describes practice, not acquired habit, automaticity, benefit, efficacy or practitioner permission. Actual enactment and context stability must be checked; outcome-dependent duration is not identity.
happeningTypes.constraints: Control, prerequisites, feasibility, legal/ethical risk and applicability NOT_ASSESSED. Behavior must be specified and independently safe/feasible; no recommendation or universal duration.

happeningTypes.name: Form a specified if-then cue-response plan
happeningTypes.description: Encode a declared anticipated situation and intended response in an if-then plan. Identity promises no enactment, associative strengthening, automaticity, efficacy, permission or enduring habit; does not include coping planning or mental contrasting by default.
happeningTypes.constraints: Actor control, goal relevance, cue occurrence, response feasibility, prerequisites, legal/ethical risk and applicability NOT_ASSESSED. No automatic practitioner recommendation.

assertions.risk: No whole automaticity or expectancy profile change, habit guarantee, universal time threshold, numerical weight or practitioner permission. Exact operation/comparator and measurement remain unresolved.
assertions.scope: Selected daily behaviors repeated at declared recurring cues; exact control-adjusted causal change in context-specific learned habit propensity not established by current source extraction.
assertions.measurement: SRHI/SRBAI or automaticity subset is a proxy with item overlap; behavioral frequency or outcome-devaluation failure alone is not independent habit strength.
assertions.timing: Daily longitudinal protocols up to84days; no fixed acquisition duration, guaranteed plateau or persistence.
assertions.mechanism: Cue-response learning is plausible, but repeated enactment, context stability, motivation and reporting are not independently manipulated in main daily-life evidence.
assertions.rationale: Longitudinal/pre-post increases and active-cue comparison do not isolate repetition's exact causal effect. Null cue-type contrast and failed lab overtraining retained as different estimands; direction remains UNKNOWN.
assertions.contributionReconciliation: One practice contribution; do not add a second automaticity effect from overlapping scale items or inferred habit→automaticity propagation.

assertions.risk: No whole automaticity or expectancy profile change, habit guarantee, universal time threshold, numerical weight or practitioner permission. Exact operation/comparator and measurement remain unresolved.
assertions.scope: Specified if-then plan in verbal cue-response tasks; exact priming measurement/controls and transfer beyond task unresolved.
assertions.measurement: Cue-prime→response-target contrast must separate association from neutral-prime→cue accessibility, word familiarity, speed/accuracy and goal success.
assertions.timing: Within-session plan encoding and later task; no months-long habit or all-context persistence.
assertions.mechanism: An encoded cue-response plan may facilitate selective response activation; reported mediation does not identify a scientific causal pathway.
assertions.rationale: Randomized planning evidence is promising but retained extraction insufficient for exact associative-strength contrast. Goal-dependent performance findings and source120 identity mismatch prevent broad signed claim.
assertions.contributionReconciliation: Plan operation, PSY-075 strength, cue accessibility, association and goal attainment cannot be summed as independent contributions; no pathway or second Family copy.
